data.title: Infliximab
data.summary: Biologicals · TNF-α inhibitor — chimeric (mouse–human) IgG1 monoclonal antibody
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Biologicals_

**Class:** TNF-α inhibitor — chimeric (mouse–human) IgG1 monoclonal antibody

## Mechanism of action
- Binds soluble and membrane-bound TNF-α with high affinity; lyses TNF-expressing cells (complement and antibody-dependent cytotoxicity)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Severe plaque psoriasis (fastest onset of TNF inhibitors), erythrodermic and generalised pustular psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis
- Pyoderma gangrenosum (especially with IBD), hidradenitis suppurativa (off-label), Behçet disease, sarcoidosis, SJS/TEN (case reports)
- Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis, rheumatoid arthritis

## Dose & formulations
- 5 mg/kg IV infusion at weeks 0, 2 and 6, then every 8 weeks (over 2 h)

## Adverse effects
- Infusion reactions (acute — fever, urticaria, hypotension; delayed serum-sickness-like)
- Antibodies against the drug (chimeric) → loss of response; methotrexate reduces this
- TB reactivation (highest risk among TNF inhibitors — often extrapulmonary/disseminated), opportunistic infections, hepatitis B reactivation
- Hepatotoxicity, demyelination, lupus-like syndrome, heart failure, hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma (young men with azathioprine)
- Paradoxical psoriasis

## Contraindications
- As for TNF inhibitors; murine protein hypersensitivity

## Drug interactions
- Other biologics; live vaccines

## Monitoring
- TB, hepatitis, HIV screening; LFT; infusion monitoring

## Pregnancy & lactation
Crosses placenta in late pregnancy (IgG1) — stop by about 16–24 weeks if possible; avoid live vaccines (BCG, rotavirus) in exposed infants for 6–12 months.

## Viva points
- Chimeric antibody — infusion reactions and antidrug antibodies
- Highest TB risk among anti-TNFs
- Fastest-acting TNF blocker in psoriasis

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.26; Khopkar (Immunobiologicals). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
